claims.text: Formation and crystal-structure selection in noble metal–based HEA nanoparticles are governed by competition between thermodynamic mixing and kinetic constraints.
Thermodynamic mixing favors formation of a single-phase solid solution.
Rapid heating and cooling kinetically lock in metastable structures.
A controlled dwell near but below the decomposition temperature permits partial atomic rearrangement and surface diffusion.
Dwell-enabled atomic rearrangement and surface diffusion promote uniform nucleation of the targeted phase before kinetic freezing.
The initial nanoparticles are metastable single-phase solid solutions produced under rapid heating and cooling.
The initial material has tendencies toward phase separation, elemental segregation, and irregular morphology.
The intervention is a controlled thermal dwell at an intermediate temperature just below significant thermal decomposition, followed by resumed rapid cooling.
Surface diffusion rates and defect density mediate atomic rearrangement during the dwell.
Dwell-induced atomic mobility reduces local concentration fluctuations and enables a more thermodynamically favorable atomic arrangement.
Reducing local concentration fluctuations lowers phase segregation and uncontrolled morphology by allowing the system to escape local kinetic traps.
Relative to continuous rapid cooling, the dwell will improve crystal-structure uniformity and may enhance FCC phase purity.
Relative to continuous rapid cooling, the dwell will reduce elemental segregation.
Relative to continuous rapid cooling, the dwell will produce more controlled particle morphology.
Rapid heating and cooling without a dwell often produce non-uniform crystal structures, phase separation, and elemental inhomogeneity because of kinetic trapping.
The proposed mechanism applies to noble metal HEAs containing at least five elements when heating and cooling rates are high enough to arrest equilibration.
The mechanism requires a narrow dwell-temperature window below the onset of phase decomposition.
The mechanism may not apply to systems with lower mixing enthalpies or to metals outside the noble metal family.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as a metastable single-phase solid solution, whereas the baseline is described as often having non-uniform crystal structures and phase separation. The distinction between a genuinely single-phase baseline and an unsuccessfully formed multiphase baseline is not resolved.
